correctness.rationale: The lambda maps are exactly the left multiplications by I+A, so the orbit at B is B+R_n(q)B. Row i of AB ranges independently over the span of rows i+1 through n of B. Thus the orbit exponent is the sum of the tail ranks. Adding row j gives q^d choices preserving dimension and q^(n-j)-q^d increasing it, with the updated dimension added to the exponent. Row 1 contributes a free factor q^(n-1); division of each point count by its orbit size is valid. Rank zero forces all other rows to vanish. The maximal profile increases at every stage; its point fraction is (1-1/q)^(n-2), giving the stated maximal count and bounding the normalized collision probability between that fraction and 1. The n=2 empty recurrence and the four row cases agree. An independent BFS on actual matrix-unit lambda maps for (n,q)=(4,2), cross-checked against B+R_n(q)B, produced 8,12,4,2 orbits of sizes 1,2,4,8, respectively, and collision probability 31/512. No uploaded script was executed.
residual_risks: The finite replay checks one action instance; the arbitrary-field and arbitrary-dimension result follows from the symbolic decomposition, not from the replay.

evidence: Theorem 3.1 gives one and only one labelled rook template in each adjoint cluster for arbitrary field. Lemma 5.1 gives the cardinality of the double orbit as the product of left and right sizes divided by their intersection size, applicable here since the actions commute.
Van Peski's random rank/corank statistic and de Melo–Kato's automorphism action are distinct; neither is the basis for this rejection.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier theorem parametrizes a partition coarser than the desired orbits, but one with an exact support-weight formula and uniform one-sided orbit size in each part. Its combination with the stated general counting lemma is covering.

evidence: For a rook support D and a corresponding template X, RX is the coordinate subspace with positions (k,j) from each (i,j) in D and k<i; XR has positions (i,l) from each (i,j) in D and l>j. Set L=sum_D(i-1), H=sum_D(n-j), and I=number of pairs (k,l),(i,j) in D with k<i and l<j. Unique rows and columns give dimensions L,H, and intersection dimension I. The two orbits through X are X+RX and X+XR, so by Yan's lemma the cluster has q^(L+H-I) points and exactly q^(H-I) left orbits of size q^L.

Every support has (q-1)^|D| differently labelled templates. Hence the exact coefficient at q^s is sum over D with L=s of (q-1)^|D| q^(H-I). Ferrara–Trombetti–Tsang already give the general component collision identity in Theorem 5.5.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This finite substitution into the pre-existing template partition and size lemma covers all n and q, not just extremal orbits or a small table. The collision statistic follows by weighting the exact histogram. Grouping the enumeration instead by tail ranks is convenient but does not create a new exact invariant.

evidence: Yan §3.1 explicitly identifies (I+aE_ij)X with adding a multiple of row j to row i; this is the frozen lambda action on the same algebra.
Right multiplication by a unitriangular matrix commutes with the left action and bijectively transports its orbits, so the left-orbit size is constant across any adjoint cluster.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A double-action classification need not in general directly classify one-sided orbit counts, but here each cluster can be divided by its common left-orbit size, and both quantities follow by local support counts on the published templates.

value.rationale: The canonical component spectrum and collision probability are naturally motivated, and the state recurrence is a convenient way to compute them. But the submitted exact-invariant advance is mechanically available from the earlier template theory and the collision identity; the extremes and fixed-n large-field estimate result from the same maximum profile. The frozen claim does not establish a distinct complexity, structural or asymptotic result that would turn this alternate enumeration into a separate advance.
residual_risks: This is a judgment on the claimed advance, not a denial of the pedagogical or computational convenience of the recurrence.
